newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: W.African central bank bill rate dips at tender.
newsitem.headline: W.African central bank bill rate dips at tender.

text.p: The Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) said the average rate on 28-day bills bought at its fifth tender of 1997 fell to 4.2088 percent from 4.4040 percent on July 7.
"This lower trend confirms that banks have ample liquidity, which should lead to a fall in the cost of credit," the central bank said in a statement after the July 14 tender.

BCEAO governor Charles Konan Banny told a news conference on July 4 he regretted that the liquidity in the banking system was not finding its way into private sector investment because bank credit was too dear, but he felt rates could fall soon.

This is the fifth tender the central bank has held this year, at weekly intervals beginning June 16, as part of its normal money market liquidity operations. During the previous months it had been injecting liquidity.
The bank sold bills worth 31.8 billion CFA francs ($53 million) after receiving offers for 36.9 billion CFA francs of paper.
It said its discount rate was unchanged at 6.25 percent.
The BCEAO is the central bank of the eight states that make up the western part of the Franc Zone -- Benin, Burkin Faso, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo.

Guinea-Bissau joined the Franc Zone in May and its currency, the peso, is in the process of being replaced by the Zone's common currency, the CFA franc. The process is due to be completed in early August.
